info.name: Grounded Brain API
info.description:
Backend API for **Grounded Brain**, a NotebookLM-style app. Users create **workspaces**, add **sources** (text, markdown, PDF, website, YouTube, web results), **chat** with them using RAG with citations, generate **learning artifacts** (summary, takeaways, flashcards, quiz, mind map, report), and keep long-term **memories**.

## How to use this collection

1. Start everything locally: `npm run dev` (Postgres, API on :8080, Inngest dev server, Prisma Studio).
2. **Run the whole collection** (Runner → Run). The folders go in order and build on each other: sign up → workspace → sources → chat → memory → artifacts → isolation checks → cleanup.
3. Or send requests one by one. IDs are saved into collection variables as you go.

"Wait until READY" requests poll in the **Collection Runner** only. When you send them by hand, re-send until the status is `READY`. Background jobs need the Inngest dev server, which `npm run dev` starts.

## Auth

Cookie sessions via Better Auth. **Sign up** or **Sign in** sets the session cookie, and Postman sends it on every later request automatically. A collection-level script adds the `Origin` header that Better Auth requires.

Each run signs up a fresh user (`user-<timestamp>@test.local`), so the collection can be re-run without conflicts.

## Responses

Every JSON response uses one envelope:

```json
{ "success": true, "data": { ... }, "message": "optional" }
{ "success": false, "error": { "code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "Workspace not found", "details": {} } }
```

- Deletes return **204** with no body. Async work (reprocess) returns **202**.
- Error codes: `BAD_REQUEST`, `VALIDATION_ERROR` (with field `details`), `UNAUTHORIZED`, `FORBIDDEN`, `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`, `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`.
- **503** means an optional integration (Cloudinary, Firecrawl, Mem0, Tavily) is not configured on the server.
- **Exception:** `POST /chat` streams an AI SDK UI message stream (server-sent events), not JSON.
- Every response has an `X-Request-Id` header. Send your own to correlate with server logs.

## Rate limits

300 requests / 15 min per IP on `/api`; 20 / min per user for chat and artifact creation; 30 / 10 min per user for uploads, imports and reprocessing. Over the limit → **429** `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS`.

## Variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | API base URL (default `http://localhost:8080`) |
| `origin` | Must match the server's `CLIENT_URL` (default `http://localhost:3000`) |
| `emailA` / `emailB` / `password` | Test users (emails are generated per run) |
| `workspaceId`, `sourceId`, `sourceId2`, `conversationId`, `memoryId`, `artifactId` | Saved automatically by the requests that create them |

exec: // Better Auth rejects cross-site POSTs without a trusted Origin.
// Every JSON response (except Better Auth's own routes) uses the { success, data | error } envelope.

item.name: 00 · Health
item.description:
Public, no auth. `/health` is an instant liveness check for load balancers. `/health/ready` probes every dependency the main flow needs, in parallel, cached for 10s:

- **Required** (503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` if any is down, with the report in `error.details`): `database`, `pinecone`, `openai`, `inngest` (dev server in development; keys in cloud mode).
- **Optional** (only `degraded`): `mem0`, `cloudinary`, `firecrawl`, `tavily`, `langfuse`.

Each check is `up`, `down`, `configured` (no free probe exists) or `not_configured`. `latencyMs` and `error` are included outside production only.

request.description: Returns `{ status: "ok" }`. No auth. Not request-logged.

exec: pm.test("required dependencies are up (status " + report.status + ")", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(200));

request.description: Checks DB, Pinecone, OpenAI, Inngest and the optional integrations. Run this first if anything else fails.

item.name: 01 · Auth
item.description: Better Auth email/password (enabled outside production). Google OAuth is also available when configured, via the browser flow at `/api/auth/sign-in/social`.

request.description: Creates user A and starts a session (sets the cookie). A fresh email is generated every run.
Signs in an existing user and sets the session cookie.
Better Auth rejects bad credentials. Does not affect the current session.
Better Auth's session endpoint: returns `{ session, user }` (not the API envelope).
The signed-in user. 401 without a session.

item.name: 02 · Workspaces
item.description: A workspace holds sources, conversations and artifacts. Every workspace route checks ownership and returns **404** for other users' workspaces.

request.description: Body: `title` (required, ≤120), `description` (≤500), `icon` (≤8 chars, e.g. an emoji), `defaultModel` (`gpt-4o-mini` | `gpt-4o`).
The user's workspaces, most recently updated first.
Partial update; at least one field is required.

item.name: 03 · Sources
item.description:
Sources are the material the workspace is grounded in. Creating one returns it as `PENDING` and queues a background job (Inngest) that extracts text, chunks it (~1000 chars, PDFs keep page numbers), embeds it and indexes it in Pinecone, then marks it `READY` (or `FAILED` with `metadata.processingError`).

Statuses: `PENDING` → `PROCESSING` → `READY` | `FAILED`.

request.description: Body: `type` (`TEXT` | `MARKDOWN`), `title` (≤200), `content`. Use the upload/import endpoints for other types.

body.raw:
{
  "type": "MARKDOWN",
  "title": "Cellular respiration",
  "content": "# Cellular respiration

Converts glucose into ATP.

- **Glycolysis**: cytoplasm
- **Krebs cycle**: mitochondrial matrix
- **Electron transport chain**: produces most ATP"
}

exec: pm.test("reached READY (requires the Inngest dev server)", () => pm.expect(status).to.eql("READY"));

request.description: In the Collection Runner this repeats every 2s until the source is `READY` (max ~90s). Sent by hand, it just shows the current status.
Summaries only: `content` is omitted (fetch one source to get it).
Query: `type` (`PDF` | `WEBSITE` | `YOUTUBE` | `TEXT` | `MARKDOWN`), `status`, `q` (searches title and content).
Full source including `content` and `metadata`.
Indexed chunks: `{ chunks: [{ index, content, tokenCount, metadata: { page? } }], count }`.
Re-runs extraction and indexing. Returns **202** immediately.
Body `{}` retries every `FAILED` source in the workspace; pass `sourceIds` to retry specific ones. Returns `{ reprocessed: <count> }`.
PDFs must go through the upload endpoint.

item.name: 04 · Sources: uploads & imports
item.description: Need the optional integrations: **Cloudinary** (PDF), **Firecrawl** (website). They return **503** when not configured. Each counts against the ingestion rate limit (30 / 10 min).

exec: pm.test("skipped: select a PDF in the 'file' field to test uploads", () => {});
pm.test("status 201 (or 503 if Cloudinary is not configured)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([201, 503]));

request.description:
**Select a PDF in the `file` field before sending.** multipart/form-data: `file` (required, PDF, ≤10 MB), `title` (optional).

The bytes are validated before storage: real `%PDF-` header, parses, ≤1000 pages, no JavaScript / launch actions / embedded files / XFA, not password-protected. Chunks keep `metadata.page`.

exec: pm.test("status 201 (or 503 if the integration is not configured)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([201, 503]));

request.description: Scrapes the page to markdown with Firecrawl. Body: `url`, optional `title`.
Imports the video transcript (the video must have captions). Body: `url`, optional `title`.
Saves a web result (e.g. one cited as `[W1]` in chat) as a source. Body: `title`, `content`, `url`.

item.name: 05 · Chat
item.description:
RAG chat over the workspace's READY sources.

**Request:** `{ messages, conversationId?, model?, webSearch? }`. Only the **latest user message** is used; history is loaded from the database, so you can send just `[latestMessage]`. Omit `conversationId` to start a new conversation.

**Response:** an AI SDK **UI message stream** (server-sent events, not JSON), plus the `X-Conversation-Id` header. The reply cites sources inline as `[1]`, `[2]` and web results as `[W1]`.

The assistant message is saved when the stream finishes, with only the citations actually used. Every 8 messages a background job updates the conversation summary and learns memories (Mem0).

request.description: Starts a new conversation. Saves its id from `X-Conversation-Id`. Optional `model`: `gpt-4o-mini` (default) or `gpt-4o`.
Same conversation. The follow-up is rewritten into a standalone search query using the history.
`webSearch: true` lets the model call Tavily. Web results are cited as `[W1]` and saved with `sourceType: "WEB"`. Silently off if Tavily is not configured.

item.name: 06 · Conversations
item.description: Saved chat threads. A conversation has `title` (auto-set from the first message), `summary` and `summaryMessageCount` (updated by the background summary job).

exec: pm.test("citations have markers", () => messages.flatMap((m) => m.citations || []).forEach((c) => pm.expect(c.marker).to.be.a("number")));

request.description: Messages in order. Assistant messages carry `citations`. **Match a citation to the `[n]` / `[Wn]` in the text by its `marker`**, not by array position. Only cited items are stored.
Optional `title`. Pass the returned id as `conversationId` in chat.

item.name: 07 · Memory
item.description: Long-term facts about the user (Mem0), injected into chat when relevant. Memories are added manually here or learned automatically from conversations. Each memory has `source`: `manual` | `learned`. Needs Mem0; returns **503** when not configured.

exec: pm.test("status 201 (or 503 if the integration is not configured)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([201, 503]));

request.description: Body: `memory` (1–2000 chars).

exec: pm.test("skipped: no memory was created (Mem0 not configured)", () => {});
pm.test("404 (or 503 if Mem0 is not configured)", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([404, 503]));

request.description: 404 when Mem0 is configured; 503 when it is not.

item.name: 08 · Artifacts
item.description:
Learning material generated from the workspace's READY sources by a background job. Creating one returns it `PENDING`; poll until `READY` (or `FAILED`).

Body: `type` (`SUMMARY` | `TAKEAWAYS` | `FLASHCARDS` | `QUIZ` | `MINDMAP` | `REPORT`), optional `title`, optional `sourceIds` (defaults to all READY sources). Returns **400** if there are no READY sources.

`content` by type: SUMMARY `{ markdown }` · TAKEAWAYS `{ items[] }` · FLASHCARDS `{ cards[{ front, back }] }` · QUIZ `{ questions[{ question, options[], correctIndex, explanation }] }` · MINDMAP `{ nodes[{ id, label }], edges[{ id, source, target }] }` · REPORT `{ markdown, sections[{ title, content }] }`.

exec: pm.test("reached READY (requires the Inngest dev server)", () => pm.expect(status).to.eql("READY"));

request.description: Polls in the Collection Runner (every 2s, max ~90s).

item.name: 09 · Cross-user isolation
item.description: Signs in as a second user (B) and confirms user A's data is invisible to them (**404**, not 403, so ids can't be probed), then signs back in as A. The session cookie switches users, so run these in order.

exec: pm.test("skipped: no memory was created (Mem0 not configured)", () => {});

request.description: Skip if Mem0 is not configured (no memory was created).

item.name: 10 · Cleanup
item.description: Deletes everything created above. Deleting a workspace also deletes its sources, conversations, artifacts and Pinecone vectors.

exec: pm.test("skipped: no memory was created (Mem0 not configured)", () => {});

request.description: Also removes the source's vectors.
Body: `sourceIds` (at least one).

item.name: 11 · Signed out (401)
item.description: Runs after sign-out: every protected route rejects requests without a session (`UNAUTHORIZED`).
